# Object classes (generated by tools/class_inventory.py)

Base: CLASS_OBJECT -107, vtable `1038:40de`. Overridden slots must be ported per class.

## Shelf item family (ported 2026-10-16)

`src/items.*` implements the shared vtable of -274/-558, the carrying variant
-337/-587, and wrapper -129. `1008:6ee6` loads the shelf rectangles from child module
-275, timer interval from -276 and maximum floor height from -277. `1008:70d4` sends
-16 to the pest on landing, -15 when a timed or shelf-positioned item is ready, and
-14 before removal. Releasing within a shelf rectangle snaps y to its bottom minus one,
z to 3000, and sets property -82. The -308 event starts a randomized -17 timer, checked
by `1008:746e` at each animation cycle's last frame (`1008:73d4`). [obs: original code,
module -81 data]

The -337/-587 variant reads its home from -524, optionally randomizing x from -526,
and switches between the tray-sized state -523 and room-sized state -108 when dragged
across the floor edge (`1008:7f16/819a/805a`). The drag origin at object +0x58 is
distinct from the actual position +0xa8; the remake now tracks both. Wrapper -129
removes itself on entering -559 if another room object has property -558
(`1010:2c1c`). [obs: original code, modules -102/-129/-338]

## Certificate and megaphone text (2026-10-16)

Class -593 reads its placement -594, three edit rectangles -51/-52/-53, font -54,
and colors -55/-56 from module -106 (`1010:47c6`). Its state-start hook
`1010:513a` bypasses the certificate when the pest already has a name, fills the
date/time controls for a newborn, saves the typed name on -595 through
`1038:6f06`, and hides controls on -4. The last-frame hook `1010:502a`
shows/focuses them; `1010:50e8` refocuses on hover. [obs: original code/data]
The remake uses an indexed-surface text overlay and `WM_CHAR` in place of the original
Win16 child edit controls. It formats a compact `dd/MM/yy` date and auto-fits it to
the narrow field; this is [inf], not a byte-exact port of the original `sShortDate`
WIN.INI formatting. Editing currently appends/backspaces ANSI-range characters,
not the full native edit-control behavior (selection, cursor motion, paste).

Class -189 has a text control read by the pest (`1038:6274` reads its +0xc2 window).
The remake now implements that typed `text()`, focus/show/hide hooks
`1010:17f4/188c/18de`, and the -203 Enter path that sends -201 via module data.
Its second original child control and exact text-control styling/layout still need
an audit of `1010:0f6e`; treat this class as partial. [obs: first text source and hooks;
inf: rendered control layout]

## Phone and caller bubble (2026-10-16)

Class -98's hover hook `1010:3f42` sends the hovered caller id -206..-210 to
the phone avatar -99, or -205 for no caller. Class -188 loads its edit rectangle
-218, font -54 and colors -55/-56 from module -188 (`1010:4062`), shows the
control when its return state -108 reaches the last frame (`1010:4488`), and
hides it on -4 (`1010:45f8`). Entering caller states -206..-210 asks the pest
for text before returning to -108 through module commands. The remake draws
wrapped GDI text into the indexed surface rather than creating a Win16 child
edit control. [obs: original hooks and ADM state data; inf: wrapping behavior]

`Pest::callerText` implements `1008:ca82`'s dispatch and the caller first-greeting
flags. -206 Pesterminator (`1008:cd8e`) picks repeat tips from -273; -208
Pestkeeper (`1008:d3e8`) chooses -272/-273 from the room-mess predicate;
-210 Pestrologer (`1008:dd66`) selects the birth-hour row, greeting first,
then predictions at list indices 1 onward. The -207 TheraPest and -209 Vet
repeat-call branches are **partial [inf]**: immediate physical illness referral
and simple Vet symptom choice work, but the original's personality, mood,
behavior-specific and random branches are not yet ported. [obs: Ghidra code,
modules -206..-210; inf: partial branch implementations]

## Wall clock (2026-10-16)

Class -90 covers the clock body -90, minute hand -89, hour hand -88, and cuckoo
-521. The body sends -519 to itself and both hands every animation cycle; its
event hook `1008:870c` refreshes local wall time (`1008:844c`) and updates only
when the minute changes. The hour hand chooses one of 25 sprites for a 12-hour
position rounded to 0, 30 or 60 minutes (`1008:854c`); the minute hand chooses
one of 24 sprites at 2.5-minute resolution (`1008:85ea`). At minute zero on a
changed hour, -90 spawns -521 (`1008:84ce`), which loops its cuckoo sprite the
current 12-hour count (`1008:8682`). [obs: code and ADM modules -88/-89/-90/-521]

The hand sprites are repeated unnamed state maps following -520. The engine's
new `enterStateAt` selects these by ordinal rather than collapsing every id=0
to the same first state. A 22:10 local-time snapshot shows H10/M10 and the
pest walking. [obs: data and headless runtime]

## Bin (2026-10-16)

Class -78's hover hook `1008:755c` iterates room objects, projects each position
into the bin runner's hit areas, and captures only objects whose anchor falls in
-158, whose held flag is set, and whose -280 property is nonzero. Capture clears
-180 (pickable) and -182 (held), sets property -1, moves the object just behind
the bin depth, and enters -160 (closing animation). Its state-end hook
`1008:773a` sends -1 to each captured object, clears the list, then enters
-161 (opening animation). [obs: original code and module -78]

The remake uses `World::objectSnapshot()` for the original world's indexed
iteration (`1038:5c38/5c60`). Headless drag of shelf bowl -85 from (180,157)
to (555,141) shows bin -160 and captured bowl at z=2899 at 2.2 seconds; at
6.5 seconds the bowl is gone and bin has returned to -108. [obs: runtime]

## Punishments, mouse and audio button (2026-10-17, Claude)

All twenty special classes are now ported. These eight live in `src/punishments.*` and
`src/room_objects.*`:

- **-92 punishment display** (`1008:eaac/ebce`): child module -529 lists the six punishment
  modules -530..-535 (their ids double as the display's picture states). -537 advances to
  the next picture unless one of them is already in the room (-538); -539 spawns the shown
  one at the pointer (`y += height/2`, z 3000), held (-182) and shown (-322). The punch
  button -93 sends -528 to switch the display on. [obs]
- **-531 16-ton weight** (`1010:0000/0144/0080`): while held above the pest's head
  (`1010:05d4`: y < pest.y − pest sprite height) and above the floor band, draw at pest.z+1;
  while falling, when it passes the head level within its half-width and the pest is on the
  floor, snap to `pest.y − list -546`, stop falling and send -293 (squash) to the pest;
  picking it up again sends -453. -423 on the pest blocks it. [obs]
- **-534 bomb** (`1010:07ea`): on its explosion message -226, if the whole pest sprite
  rectangle lies inside the explosion sprite rectangle (`1038:1aac` on both pest corners),
  send -26 to the pest. [obs]
- **-550 cannonball** (`1010:0b8e/0d10`): remembers whether it starts left of the pest; when
  it passes the pest's x with vertical overlap and |Δz| ≤ list -551, it moves to the pest
  (+ offset list -552) and enters -553. [obs]
- **-172 cannon** (`1010:6986`): hover event -555 sets its x to the pointer; -556 fires —
  spawns -534 at the pointer (z 3999) and detonates it with -446 if the pointer is on the
  pest, else spawns -557. The terminator button -97 spawns the cannon. [obs]
- **-591 flea powder** (`1010:3c0a/3d0a`): while held above the pest within its sprite width,
  enter/loop -592 (which sends -448 flea spray); otherwise stop looping. [obs]
- **-91 mouse** (`1008:77da..7eae`, shelf item subclass): runs between its hole -320 and the
  edges from list -318 (−100, 740); -324 starts a run, end of -325 at the hole enters -328,
  -327 stops it, -1 returns it to -321. [obs]
- **-94 audio button** (`1010:06f8`): -164 off, -163 on, -162 picks the current setting;
  the flag is `theApp+0xcc` (INI `[Options] Audio`) and mutes the mixer. [obs; INI not read yet]

Verified headlessly: punch button → 16-ton picture → drag the weight above the pest and release
→ pest -293 (PPSQUASH, feet under the weight); terminator button → cannon rises, follows the
pointer, firing on the pest shows the explosion and the pest then runs off (-468); audio button
toggles AUDIOON/AUDIOOFF.
